notes: Stack: Django 4.1.2 + DRF + channels (GeoDjango/PostGIS, Firebase, Google Analytics) - a backend with a small web UI, not a JS front-end. Ran on Python 3.9 with SQLite and 21 seeded sample users (8 clients, 3 admins, 10 drivers with status/rating/trips; fictional names, placeholder +2499000001xx numbers). Shown page is the project's own 'User Statistics' admin page (dashboard_app/templates/user_stats.html), template untouched; the two charts and the rest of the Drivers table are below the fold. Changes confined to the run copy: database pointed at SQLite instead of the remote PostGIS server; because this machine has no GDAL/GEOS, django.contrib.gis was replaced by a small stand-in module (PointField stored as text) and the gis apps removed from INSTALLED_APPS; Firebase initialisation skipped and the service-account file deleted from the copy (never read or used). Doubts: (1) the public landing page at / is byte-identical to the one in 'Services Platform' (same wrapper.html), so it was not used as the main shot to avoid two identical portfolio images - it is available at web/truckgo-web-home-alt.png (laid out at 1280px) if the owner prefers the landing page here. (2) /dashboard/ is the unmodified Sneat demo admin template (stock 'Congratulations John' content, 'Upgrade to Pro' button), so it was deliberately not shown. (3) The stats page is visually plain (bare Bootstrap); the charts further down still carry leftover sample titles ('World Wine Production 2023') in the project's own template - they are outside the captured area.
